facts.fact: The Acting Chief Registrar says the Judiciary's Case Management System (JSDS2) has been in place since 2018.
The Judiciary says the new Electronic Case Management System (e-CMS), now fully built to replace JSDS2, has been in trial in all courts since 2 October 2023, with use to start on 1 November 2023.

The Judiciary's Chief Court Administrator named the Judiciary Electronic Case Management System (JoT e-CMS) among its platforms, and the ICT Centre director said Judiciary systems interface with 16 national institutions, enabling real-time tracking of all registered and adjudicated cases from the Court of Appeal to District Courts.

facts.fact: Chief Court Administrator Elisante Ole Gabriel said the judiciary's electronic case management system is gradually phasing out paper-based files, and is being expanded.
Chief Court Administrator Elisante Ole Gabriel said litigants can now file cases online from anywhere and track case progress.

facts.fact: Deputy Registrar Richard Kabate writes in The Guardian that the Electronic Case Management System (e-CMS) was expanded across more courts during Chief Justice Masaju's first year to June 2026.

Chief Registrar Eva Nkya said on 3 March 2026 that the Judiciary's electronic case management system JOT-eCMS operates from District Courts up to the Court of Appeal and is integrated with ten stakeholder systems, six more being linked.

systems.tiers: District Courts to Court of Appeal; Primary Courts use a separate platform

facts.fact: Government Notice 609 of 2025, signed by the Chief Justice on 16 October 2025, amends the Electronic Filing Rules so a document filed electronically is deemed filed on its filing date once the court fee is paid within seven days of the bill, and is otherwise rejected.

systems.country_label: Judiciary electronic filing under the Electronic Filing Rules

facts.fact: Judiciary chief executive Elisante Ole Gabriel said at the e-Government meeting of 17-19 February 2026 that the Electronic Case Management System is being implemented to end paper files, and that citizens can now file a case from anywhere and see which magistrate has it.
The judiciary's chief executive said in February 2026 that a citizen can now open a case from wherever they are, under the Electronic Case Management System (e-GA feature).
